recipes.title: Air Fryer Brussels Sprouts with Bacon
steps: Crisp the bacon lardons and jar them with their fat.
Toss the sprouts with the bacon fat, lard and salt.
Air fry at 400°F in two batches, 15 minutes each, shaking halfway.
Toss with the bacon, pepper and cider vinegar.
recipes.notes: Sprouts halved and bacon crisped the day before.

recipes.title: Apple Cider Doughnut Focaccia

ingredients: 200 g sourdough discard, 100% hydration, cold and unfed is fine
groups.name: Dough

ingredients: 30 g olive oil, for the pan
groups.name: To bake and finish

steps: Warm the cinnamon sticks in a dry skillet over medium heat, 1 to 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Cool, break up and grind the cinnamon in a spice grinder. Sift.
Mix the ground cinnamon with the sugar and 1 g salt. Store airtight.
Mix the flour, discard, water, cider reduction, 12 g salt, yeast, ground cinnamon and 40 g olive oil until no dry flour remains.
With a wet hand, lift and fold the dough over itself 4 times, rotating the bowl.
Repeat the folds 3 more times at 30 minute intervals.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, 12 to 24 hours, toward the back of the fridge.
Pour 30 g olive oil into the pan, transfer the dough and turn to coat.
Proof at room temperature until puffy and relaxed to the edges, 2 to 3 hours.
Heat the oven to 425F.
Dimple the dough to the bottom of the pan with oiled fingers.
Bake 22 to 28 minutes, until deep golden and pulling from the sides.
Turn out, brush all over with the melted butter and press the top and sides into the cinnamon sugar.
recipes.notes: Serve with the cider cream cheese glaze for dipping. For a 36 hour cold ferment, use 2 g yeast instead of 3 g.

recipes.title: Banana Boats
steps: Split each banana lengthwise through the peel without cutting through the bottom.
Stuff with marshmallows, chocolate chips, peanut butter chips and walnuts.
Wrap in foil.
Cook 10 minutes in the coals.

recipes.title: Barbacoa (Crockpot)

ingredients: 4 dried guajillo chiles, toasted, stemmed and seeded
4 dried ancho chiles, toasted, stemmed and seeded
2 dried morita chiles, toasted and stemmed
2 chipotles in adobo plus 30 g adobo sauce
groups.name: Chiles

ingredients: 2.5 lb beef chuck roast, cut into large chunks
groups.name: Braise

steps: Toast the guajillo, ancho and morita in a dry pan over medium, 20 to 30 seconds a side, with the vent running.
Soak the toasted chiles in hot water 20 minutes.
Blend the soaked chiles with the chipotles, adobo, onion, garlic, broth, vinegar, cumin, oregano and salt until smooth.
Sear the chuck hard in a skillet.
Deglaze the skillet into the crockpot.
Add the beef, sauce and bay leaves to the crockpot.
Cook on low 8 hours.
Lift the meat out with a slotted spoon.
Skim the fat from the liquid and pull the bay leaves.
Reduce the liquid hard in a wide saucepan, 15 minutes or more, until it coats a spoon and a finger track across the back holds.
Taste the reduced sauce for salt.
Shred the meat and toss with enough sauce to coat; jar any extra sauce.
Cool on a sheet pan.
Split in half: one half to the fridge, the other wrapped flat and frozen.
At camp, reheat in a foil pan.
recipes.notes: Frozen half rides as cooler ballast and is used two days later. Excess liquid boils foil-packet fillings, so reduce before splitting.

recipes.title: Beer-Battered Walleye and Chips

ingredients: 1.35 kg walleye fillets, thawed, skinned, cut crosswise into 14 pieces of about 3 oz
groups.name: Fish

ingredients: two 28 oz bags frozen thick-cut chips
groups.name: Chips

steps: Whisk the dry mix ingredients together and bag.
Heat the oil in an 8-quart stockpot to 190°C, lid on while it climbs and between batches.
Air fry the chips at 400°F in batches, 15 to 18 minutes, shaking halfway.
Salt the chips the second they come out and hold on a rack in a 200°F oven.
Whisk the lager and vodka into the dry mix just to combine, lumps and all. Rest 10 minutes.
Pat the fish dry and salt both sides.
Dredge in flour, shake off, dip in batter and let the excess run.
Lower away from yourself into the 190°C oil.
Fry 3 to 4 minutes, three or four pieces at a time, until the batter is hard and deep gold. Fry the thin tail pieces together.
Drain on a rack and salt immediately.
Serve with malt vinegar and tartar sauce.
recipes.notes: Dry mix made days ahead. Fried outdoors on an induction burner. Cool the oil fully before storing.

recipes.title: Big-Batch Dill and Escabeche Pickle Soup with Mushrooms
recipes.yield: fills an 8 qt pot, about 12 servings

ingredients: 700 g smoked kielbasa, sliced into half-moons (optional)
1500 g Yukon Gold potatoes, 2 cm dice
60 g fresh dill, stems tied with twine, fronds chopped
groups.name: Base

ingredients: 100 g dill-pickled cauliflower, chopped to 1 cm
75 g dill-pickled green beans, cut to 1 cm
75 g dill-pickled fennel, chopped to 1 cm
groups.name: Pickles and brine

ingredients: 3 g Diamond Crystal kosher salt, to taste
groups.name: Seasoning

ingredients: 75 g prepared horseradish, not creamy style (optional)
groups.name: To finish

steps: Cover the porcini with the hot water and soak until soft, about 20 minutes.
Lift out the porcini and chop them. Strain the soaking liquid through a paper towel, leaving any grit behind.
Melt 60 g of the butter in an 8 qt stockpot over medium-high heat. Brown the kielbasa, then remove with a slotted spoon.
Brown the cremini in two batches in the remaining fat, adding the rest of the butter for the second batch. Set aside with the kielbasa.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook until softened, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, oregano (crushed between your palms) and cumin. Stir until fragrant.
Add the potatoes, stock, chopped porcini and strained soaking liquid, bay leaves, allspice and tied dill stems.
Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes are fork-tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in all the pickled vegetables, both brines, the kielbasa and cremini, and the pepper.
Add as much of the reserve stock as fits while leaving about 1 inch of headspace. Simmer 10 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves, allspice and dill stems.
Stir in the MSG and taste. Add more brine for sourness and the salt only if needed.
Ladle the portions to be frozen into containers before adding the sour cream.
Whisk the sour cream, flour and horseradish, scaled to the soup left in the pot.
Whisk in 2 ladles of hot broth, then stir the mixture back into the pot.
Heat gently without boiling until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the chopped dill fronds and serve.
recipes.notes: Freeze portions without the sour cream for up to 3 months. To serve frozen portions, thaw, reheat, then temper in about 40 g sour cream, 2.5 g flour and 6 g horseradish per serving, and finish with fresh dill. For one quart served fresh: 65 g sour cream, 4 g flour, 10 g horseradish, 8 g dill fronds. Serve with buttered, toasted rye.

recipes.title: Braised Red Cabbage

ingredients: 75 g cider vinegar, plus a splash to finish
2 whole cloves, or a scant 1/8 tsp ground

steps: Soften the onion in the butter.
Add everything else and toss to coat.
Cover and cook on low 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
Uncover and cook off the liquid, 15 minutes, stirring often so it doesn't catch.
Pull out the cinnamon stick, and the cloves if whole.
Taste and correct salt and vinegar. It should be sharp.
Cool and refrigerate.
To serve, reheat in a covered pot on low, stirring now and then.
Taste and sharpen with a splash of cider vinegar.
recipes.notes: Made 3 days ahead; reheated on low about 4 hours before dinner.

recipes.title: Broiled Salsa Verde
steps: Line a sheet pan with foil, not parchment.
Arrange the tomatillos cut side down with the jalapeños, onion and garlic.
Broil about 4 inches from the element, about 10 minutes, until blackened in spots.
Peel the garlic.
Blend everything, including the liquid pooled on the pan.
Refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Better after a day. Came out hotter than intended with 2 jalapeños; sour cream at the table mutes it.

recipes.title: Buffalo Chicken Hand Pies

ingredients: 1 bottle (12 oz) Frank's RedHot Buffalo Wings Sauce
groups.name: Filling

ingredients: 1 box puff pastry (2 sheets), thawed in the fridge
4 oz blue cheese crumbles (for half the pies)
groups.name: Pastry

steps: Season the thighs with salt and a little oil and roast at 400°F 25 to 30 minutes, to 175°F.
Shred while warm, using a stand mixer with the paddle on low.
Cook the shredded chicken with the sauce, cooking off about a quarter, until no free liquid runs when a chilled spoonful is tilted.
Season with cayenne.
Cool completely.
Fold in the cream cheese, cheddar and celery seed.
Chill overnight.
Cut the puff pastry into 12 pieces and portion the cold filling onto them.
Fold, seal hard with a fork, and cut two vent slits.
Freeze raw on a sheet pan, then bag.
On baking day, brush the frozen pies with egg wash.
Press blue cheese crumbles onto the tops of half the pies.
Bake from frozen at 400°F for 28 to 30 minutes.
Cool completely on a rack before packing in a rigid container.
recipes.notes: Raw assembled pies freeze until baking. After baking, refrigerate in a rigid container; do not refreeze. Eat early on day of travel and keep cold in a dry bag with a frozen bottle.

recipes.title: Cabbage-Carrot Slaw with Sumac Dressing
steps: Shred the cabbage and julienne the carrots; bag together dry and undressed.
Dissolve the sugar in the lemon juice.
Add the oil, sumac, Aleppo, Cointreau, salt and pepper to a jar and shake.
Dress the slaw at serving time.
recipes.notes: Store vegetables and dressing separately until serving. Dressing keeps in a sealed jar.

recipes.title: Cajun Runoff Butter

ingredients: ~250 ml pooled butter runoff from the boil toss
10 g Crystal hot sauce (15 g for genuinely hot)

steps: Pour ~250 ml of the pooled runoff from the toss into a bowl.
Stir in the Cajun seasoning and cayenne.
Stir in the Crystal, poured from the bottle.
recipes.notes: Pre-mix the Cajun seasoning and cayenne in one container; keep the Crystal separate.

recipes.title: Camp Breakfast Burritos (Cheesy Sausage)

ingredients: 20 oz (567 g) refrigerated diced potatoes with peppers and onion

steps: Cook the potatoes in an uncrowded pan until genuinely browned, not just heated through.
Salt the potatoes and cool completely.
Scramble the eggs soft and slightly underdone; cool completely.
Brown the sausage and drain most of the fat.
Off the heat, tear in the American cheese and stir until it coats the sausage.
Cool the sausage completely.
Warm one tortilla in a dry skillet 15 to 20 seconds a side.
Fill with about 6 oz of potatoes, eggs, sausage and cheddar, and roll tight.
Repeat with each tortilla, warming one at a time.
Wrap each in foil and freeze flat.
At camp, set the frozen burritos at the edge of the coal bed, not buried, 15 to 20 minutes, turning twice.
recipes.notes: Frozen burritos ride as cooler ballast. Hot sauce on the side.

recipes.title: Camp Cheesesteaks (Shaved Chuck Eye with Queso)

ingredients: 2040 g shaved chuck eye, portioned at home into 8 portions of 255 g

steps: Cook the mushrooms on the griddle dry and hot, undisturbed, until their water cooks off.
Finish the mushrooms with butter and salt and hold in a foil pan near the fire.
Reheat the queso in the dutch oven at the edge of the coals until molten.
Cook the onions on the griddle, adding the peppers a few minutes later, then push to one side.
Put the meat on the cleared hot surface and chop with two spatulas.
When just past pink, pile it, fold in the onions and peppers, and add provolone if using; let it slump 30 seconds.
Toast the rolls face-down on the edge of the griddle.
Scoop the meat into the rolls and spoon queso over the top.
Wrap in paper, tape, rest 2 minutes, and cut through the paper.
Keep a plain corner of meat with no onion or pepper for kids.
recipes.notes: Portion the meat at home with a scale so nothing is weighed at camp.

recipes.title: Camp Hot Chocolate (Swiss Miss and Half-and-Half)

ingredients: 12 servings Swiss Miss, per the canister scoop
3 cups half-and-half, cold (725 g if pre-measuring)
spiced rum or Baileys, for adults
groups.name: At the mug

steps: Pre-warm the airpot: boiling water in, 5 minutes, dump.
Boil the water in the stainless pot.
Whisk in the Swiss Miss.
Stir in the cold half-and-half off the heat.
Fill the airpot.
recipes.notes: Lands around 68°C, hot but drinkable. Nothing scorches since the water does the heating. Needs about a 3 qt pot.

recipes.title: Campfire Dutch Oven Cornbread (Jiffy)

ingredients: 4 boxes Jiffy corn muffin mix, combined in one bag
600 g milk and 4 eggs, whisked together in one container
Honey and butter for the table

steps: Preheat the bare cast iron dutch oven with the lard, swirled to coat the bottom and 5 cm up the sides, until it shimmers.
Pour the wet mix in, dump the Jiffy on top, stir fast, and put the lid on.
Set a third of the coals underneath and two-thirds on the lid.
Rotate the pot a quarter turn every 10 minutes.
Bake 25 to 35 minutes, checking at 25.
Home oven method: preheat an enameled dutch oven dry at 220°C for 15 minutes once the oven is up.
Home oven method: add the lard, swirl, and return to the oven 3 to 4 minutes to heat the fat.
Home oven method: pour in the wet mix, dump in the Jiffy, stir fast, and level.
Home oven method: bake uncovered 30 to 40 minutes, checking at 30, until golden and a skewer comes out clean; tent with foil if the top browns early.
Rest 10 minutes before cutting.
recipes.notes: Wet mix and dry mix are prepped and stored separately until baking.

recipes.title: Campfire Foil Packet Bar

ingredients: 1 head cabbage, outer leaves whole plus 1 cm rounds
groups.name: Liner and base

ingredients: 14 oz plain smoked ham, 15 mm dice
groups.name: Proteins

ingredients: 8 oz Velveeta, cut into 1.5 cm cubes
Creole seasoning, chili flakes, hot sauce, salsa verde, salsa roja
groups.name: Finish

steps: Build the fire at least 90 minutes ahead so there is a bed of coals.
Lay heavy-duty 18-inch foil double, and line each packet with cabbage.
Add tots straight from the cooler.
Add proteins, beans and vegetables to taste.
Add a pat of butter to every packet.
Lay cheese cubes on top of the fillings.
Seal and write names on the foil with a Sharpie.
Cook in the coals about 20 minutes, flipping once; never open packets on the fire.
Grill backup: 200°C, lid down, 20 to 25 minutes, flipped once.

recipes.title: Campfire Stovetop Popcorn
steps: Put an 8 qt pot with a lid over the fire.
Add the oil and 3 kernels.
When those pop, add the rest of the kernels.
Take the pot off the heat 30 seconds, then return it and shake steadily.
Pull when the popping slows to a few seconds between pops.
Salt immediately while steaming.
recipes.notes: Weights are for pre-measuring at home.

recipes.title: Carnitas (Oven, Dutch Oven)

ingredients: 3.3 lb bone-in pork shoulder butt, cut into 5 cm chunks around the bone
groups.name: Braise

steps: Put everything in an enameled dutch oven with the orange peels and the bone.
Add water to come halfway up the meat.
Cover and cook at 165°C for 3 hours.
Uncover, raise to 190°C, and cook about 30 minutes until the liquid renders down and the edges catch.
Pull the bone.
Shred coarsely, keeping some fat with the meat.
Cool on a sheet pan; skim and jar any fat that separates.
Split evenly: 542 g to the fridge, 542 g wrapped flat and frozen.
At camp, heat the griddle, add the lard, spread the meat in a thin layer, and leave it 2 to 3 minutes before turning.
recipes.notes: Frozen half rides as cooler ballast. The braise needs no added fat; the shoulder renders its own.

recipes.title: Charred Broccoli and Cauliflower
steps: Cut florets about 4 cm, with a flat face cut on each; cut the cauliflower slightly smaller.
Heat a cast iron skillet on the fire until ripping hot and dry.
Add the cauliflower flat side down for 4 minutes.
Add the broccoli and leave everything undisturbed until blackened in spots, 4 to 5 minutes.
Toss and cook a few minutes more.
Off the heat, toss with the oil and salt.
Finish with lemon, flaky salt and pepper; serve chili flakes on the side.

recipes.title: Cheese, Onion and Potato Pasties

ingredients: 2 g fresh thyme leaves, finely chopped
2 eggs, beaten (1 for sealing, 1 with a splash of water for egg wash)

steps: Boil the potato in salted water 5 minutes, drain and cool.
Soften the onion in the butter 8 minutes and cool.
Combine everything but the egg.
Taste cold and salt again.
Fill one half of each round, egg the border, fold, rope crimp and cut a vent.
Freeze on a tray, then bag.
To bake, heat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.
Space the pasties out from frozen.
Brush all over with egg wash, keeping it out of the vents.
Bake 45 minutes, until deep golden and 165°F in the middle.
Rest 10 minutes. Serve with piccalilli and English mustard.
recipes.notes: Bake straight from frozen.

recipes.title: Chole (Punjabi Chickpea Curry)

ingredients: 1 black tea bag (or a couple dried amla)
groups.name: Chickpeas

ingredients: anardana (dried pomegranate seed), toasted and ground
groups.name: Masala

steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight.
Pressure-cook the chickpeas with the tea bag (or amla) for color.
Brown the onions properly.
Add tomatoes and cook down until the oil separates.
Add the spices, anardana, and amchur, then the chickpeas.
Crush in kasuri methi at the end.
Finish with a ghee tadka of ginger julienne and green chili.
Salt boldly.

recipes.title: Cider Cream Cheese Glaze

ingredients: 30 g cider reduction, plus more to thin

steps: Beat the cream cheese and butter until smooth.
Beat in the powdered sugar, cider reduction and salt.
Thin with more reduction until dippable.
Refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Make a day ahead. Take out the morning of serving to soften. Serve in a bowl beside the focaccia for dipping, not spread on top.

recipes.title: Cider Reduction
steps: Simmer the cider in a wide pan until reduced to about 150 g, thick and syrupy.
Weigh it in a tared heatproof cup; if it reduced past 150 g, stir water back in while warm to bring it to 150 g.
Cover, cool and refrigerate.
recipes.notes: 120 g goes in the apple cider doughnut focaccia and 30 g in the cider cream cheese glaze. Warm slightly to loosen if it sets firm in the fridge.

recipes.title: Classic Homemade Steak Sauce
steps: Whisk everything together in a small saucepan until smooth.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat and cook about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Taste and adjust vinegar, brown sugar and hot sauce.
Cool slightly before serving.
recipes.notes: Keeps 2 to 3 weeks refrigerated in a sealed jar; better after a day or two.

recipes.title: Cocktail Sauce
steps: Stir everything together.
Refrigerate.
Taste after a day and add more horseradish if it has mellowed.
recipes.notes: Holds two weeks refrigerated and improves sitting. Let it sit an hour before judging the heat.

recipes.title: Cornbread Breakfast Sandwiches
steps: Split cornbread wedges horizontally.
Griddle the cut sides in butter or lard until crisp.
Fry the eggs with jammy yolks.
Stack: cornbread, pimento cheese, egg, pepper jelly, cornbread.

recipes.title: Creole Mustard

ingredients: 20 g yellow mustard seeds (or 80 g brown total and no yellow)

steps: Combine the mustard seeds, vinegar, and water in a jar.
Cover with a regular lid and leave at room temperature about 24 hours, stirring once or twice, until the seeds absorb most of the liquid; add a splash of water if they look dry.
Blend about half the mixture with an immersion blender in a tall narrow container until creamy, leaving the rest whole.
Stir both halves back together.
Stir in the horseradish, salt, and cayenne.
Seal and refrigerate 2 days before using.
recipes.notes: Keeps 3 months refrigerated.

recipes.title: Creole Mustard Slaw
recipes.yield: enough for 4 French bread loaves of po'boys
steps: Toss the cabbage with the mayonnaise, Creole mustard, vinegar, and salt.
Refrigerate about 30 minutes.
Serve on warmed, crisped French bread loaves piled with pulled cochon de lait.

recipes.title: Cubano Tater Tot Casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 425F. Grease a 9x13 pan.
In a large skillet over high heat, brown the pork, breaking it up, until well browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, oregano, salt, and the lime zest and juice.
Add the orange juice and cook until the liquid is gone, about 4 minutes.
Transfer to a bowl with the ham.
In the same pan over medium heat, melt the butter. Cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the flour and cook, stirring, 2 to 3 minutes until it smells nutty.
Warm the milk. Whisk it in gradually, bring to a simmer, and cook, stirring often, 12 to 15 minutes, until it coats the back of a spoon.
Off heat, stir in the Swiss, mustard, pickle brine, salt and pepper until smooth.
Fold the ham, pork and chopped pickles into the sauce. Spread in the pan.
Arrange the tots on top in a single tight layer.
Melt the butter with the grated garlic and salt. Drizzle evenly over the tots.
Bake about 30 minutes, until the tots are deep golden and the sauce is bubbling at the edges.
Scatter the Swiss over the top and bake about 5 minutes until melted.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes: Serve with extra pickle spears and yellow mustard.

recipes.title: Dill Pickle Jar (Pickle Bowls)

ingredients: 350 g okra, whole, stem cap trimmed
350 g green beans, trimmed to jar height
groups.name: Vegetables
Brine (half of the shared 2.4 L batch)

steps: Cut everything thick.
Pack the vegetables and aromatics raw into the jar, upright.
Simmer the vinegar, water, salt and sugar until dissolved.
Cool the brine to warm, not boiling.
Pour over the vegetables.
Run a chopstick down the sides to release air bubbles, then top up.
Seal and refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Best 5 to 6 days out; made Mon 8/31 or Tue 9/1 for a 9/6 serve. A bay leaf or pinch of black tea per jar helps crunch. Does not need a cooler in transit. Combine with the escabeche jar into shared bowls at serving.

recipes.title: Dill Pickle Potato Salad

ingredients: 60 g kosher salt, for the cooking water
2.7 kg Yukon Gold potatoes, skins on, cut in 1.5 cm pieces
340 g refrigerated dill pickles, diced at 6 mm, drained
groups.name: Salad

steps: Soak the minced shallot in pickle brine or cider vinegar 10 minutes.
Whisk the dressing ingredients together.
Boil the potatoes in water salted with the 60 g kosher salt until fork-tender, about 10 minutes.
Drain and let steam off 2 minutes.
Dress the potatoes while warm, mashing some as you stir.
Cool.
Fold in the pickles, shallot, dill and eggs.
Refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Made 2 days ahead. Stir before storing and again the next morning. Taste the morning of serving and loosen with mayo and pickle brine if it has tightened.

recipes.title: Drawn Lemon Butter
steps: Melt the butter in a small pan.
Stir in the lemon juice.
Keep warm until serving.
recipes.notes: Made ahead and remelted day of, after the endive boats while the pot climbs.

recipes.title: Duck Fat Roast Potatoes

ingredients: 2.2 kg yellow potatoes, peeled and quartered
salt, for heavily salted boiling water

steps: Boil the potatoes in heavily salted water 8 minutes.
Drain and shake hard in the pot to rough up the edges.
Toss with the duck fat and 25 g kosher salt.
Cool and refrigerate in a covered pan.
Spread across two sheet pans and roast under the hens at 425°F.
When the hens come out, finish the potatoes alone at 450°F for 20 minutes, turning once.
Scatter with rosemary and more salt.
recipes.notes: Parboiled and fat-coated up to 3 days ahead.

recipes.title: Duck Fat Rösti

ingredients: 1.1 kg russet potatoes, whole and unpeeled

steps: Parboil the whole unpeeled russets 10 minutes, until tender at the edge and firm in the middle.
Cool, peel and grate coarsely. Bag and refrigerate.
Toss the grated potato with the salt and pepper.
Heat the duck fat in a 12-inch cast iron skillet.
Press the potato in flat, about 2 cm deep.
Cook over medium 12 minutes, until the underside is deep brown.
Tilt the skillet and spoon the loose fat into a heatproof bowl.
Slide the rösti onto the flat underside of an upside-down sheet pan, put the skillet over it and flip both together.
Spoon the fat back in around the edges.
Cook 10 minutes more.
Cut in 8 wedges and salt again.
recipes.notes: Potato parboiled and grated up to 3 days ahead (Tuesday for Friday).

recipes.title: Escabeche Pickle Jar (Pickle Bowls)

ingredients: 600 ml apple cider vinegar (sherry vinegar for any shortfall)
groups.name: Brine (half of the shared 2.4 L batch)

steps: Cut everything thick.
Pack the vegetables and aromatics raw into the jar, with a dense layer of carrots across the top to hold the radish and jalapeño down.
Simmer the vinegar, water, salt and sugar until dissolved.
Cool the brine to warm, not boiling.
Pour over the vegetables.
Run a chopstick down the sides to release air bubbles, then top up.
Seal and refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Best 5 to 6 days out. The radish turns this jar pink. Does not need a cooler in transit.

recipes.title: Frozen Chocolate Milk Slushie (112 oz)
steps: Whisk everything together.
Refrigerate.
Pour in cold.
Run on the Milkshake preset.
recipes.notes: Made ahead at home and kept cold in the cooler.

recipes.title: Frozen Limeade Slushie (112 oz)

ingredients: 830 g frozen limeade concentrate (about 2 1/3 cans, 12 oz each)

steps: Stir until the concentrate dissolves.
Refrigerate.
Pour in cold.
Run on the Slush preset.
recipes.notes: Three parts water to one part concentrate (not label strength), which puts sugar near 14 percent. If using bottled limeade instead, add simple syrup to get it near 14 percent sugar.

recipes.title: Garlic Old Bay Butter
steps: Melt the butter over low heat.
Add the garlic and cook 4 to 6 minutes until it smells sweet rather than sharp, without browning.
Take off the heat.
Stir in the Old Bay, paprika, lemon juice and pepper.
Cool, then bag it flat and freeze.
Day of: melt over low heat, stirring; do not let it boil.
At the pull, stir in ~500 ml boil liquor before tossing.
recipes.notes: Frozen flat in a half-inch slab it remelts in minutes. Milk solids separate on melting and reintegrate when stirred. Made the week of Aug 25 and frozen.

recipes.title: Garlic-Dill Yogurt Sauce
steps: Mix all ingredients.
Refrigerate at least a few hours before serving.
recipes.notes: Better on day two. Raw garlic strengthens over two days. Holds Thursday to Saturday in a cooler.

recipes.title: Go Juice (Liquid IV and Caffeine Stick Station)

ingredients: Liquid IV packets, Firecracker Popsicle flavor
CELSIUS On-the-Go sticks (200 mg caffeine, Berry or Cranberry Lemon), one 14-pack
Pure Kick Blue Raspberry sticks (80 mg caffeine), one 72-pack

steps: Set the Liquid IV packets and caffeine sticks out next to the water.
Each person mixes one Liquid IV packet with water.
Add one caffeine stick to taste: a CELSIUS stick for about 200 mg, or Pure Kick sticks at 80 mg each.
recipes.notes: Label the caffeine amounts per stick. Plain water and other electrolyte options alongside.

recipes.title: Green Room Freezer Martini
recipes.yield: 52.5 oz, about 17 pours at 3 oz, about 32% ABV
steps: Dissolve the salt in the water.
Combine everything at room temperature in a 64 oz jar.
Stir well.
Freeze at least 6 hours.
Pour 3 oz straight into a frozen glass, no ice, no stirring.
Garnish with a grapefruit twist, or a lime twist for sharper.
recipes.notes: Citrus-free, so it keeps indefinitely in the freezer. It goes cloudy in the cold. Taste a pour before adding any more Fernet (3 oz is the ceiling).

recipes.title: Grilled Vegetable Skewers
recipes.yield: about 20 skewers, serves 10 to 12 as a side

ingredients: 2 yellow summer squash, cut into coins
5 bell peppers, red or orange, cut into squares slightly smaller than the coins
1 1/2 lb cremini mushrooms, whole, wiped not washed
groups.name: Vegetables (all cut to about 3/4 inch)

steps: Up to 2 days ahead, cut all vegetables and store dry and unsalted in the fridge; keep mushrooms whole in paper.
At camp, stir the Aleppo into the oil and let it sit a few minutes.
Toss each vegetable in its own bowl with enough oil to look glossy, then salt and pepper.
Thread onto bamboo skewers without crowding; skewer mushrooms through the side of the cap.
Hang the handle ends past the edge of the grate, away from the heat.
Grill over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes, turning 2 or 3 times, until colored and the squash gives slightly.
Grill the lemon halves cut side down on a clean oiled grate 3 to 5 minutes, undisturbed, until deeply browned.
Off the heat, squeeze the warm charred lemon over the skewers.
Drizzle with olive oil, and balsamic glaze if using.
recipes.notes: Cut vegetables keep 2 days refrigerated if stored dry and unsalted. Salt and oil go on only at the grill.

recipes.title: Growler Toasted Almond Revolver
recipes.yield: about 59 oz in a 64 oz growler, about 16 pours at 3.7 oz, about 28% ABV

ingredients: 1/2 oz Fernet-Branca or another bitter amaro
heaping 1/4 tsp fine salt (two big pinches)

steps: Empty the growler into a large pitcher or bowl.
Stir in the bourbon, cold brew, water and amaro.
Add the bitters and salt and stir until the salt dissolves.
Taste, and add more bitters or a pinch more salt if it reads cloying.
Funnel back into the growler, cap, and refrigerate at least 4 hours.
Pour about 3.7 oz over one large cube.
Express an orange peel over the top and drop it in.
recipes.notes: No citrus or dairy, keeps 3 to 4 weeks refrigerated. Optional: small tinctures in 2 oz bourbon each (one cracked cinnamon stick for 2 days; 4 or 5 cloves for 24 hours; peel of one orange for 4 hours), strained, dosed by the drop per glass or into the batch a day before serving.

recipes.title: Gruyere and Gouda Grilled Cheese
steps: Toss the cheeses together.
Butter one side of each slice.
Build the sandwiches buttered sides out, with the cheese mounded to the edges.
Cook over medium-low, covered, until deep golden and fully melted, 4 to 5 minutes per side.
recipes.notes: Served with the tomato soup.

recipes.title: Hot Chocolate from Ganache Base (Camp Airpot)
steps: Heat the cream.
Pour over the chopped chocolate.
Rest 2 minutes, then whisk smooth.
Whisk in the cocoa, sugar, vanilla and salt.
Jar it. Yields about 500 g.
At camp, pre-warm the airpot: boiling water in, 5 minutes, dump.
Heat the milk to 70°C in the stainless pot at the edge of the coals, stirring, off direct flame.
Whisk in the ganache until smooth.
Fill the airpot.
Serve marshmallows and whipped cream at the mug, never in the airpot.
recipes.notes: Milk scorches: keep it moving and off direct flame.

recipes.title: Irish Lamb Stew

ingredients: 1.4 kg boneless lamb shoulder, cut in 4 cm pieces
500 g russet potatoes, peeled, cut small
1.1 kg red potatoes, peeled, cut in large chunks
groups.name: Stew

ingredients: about 1 L chicken stock, to thin
groups.name: To reheat and serve

steps: Season the lamb hard with half the salt and half the pepper.
Brown it in lard in batches in a Dutch oven, removing each batch.
Soften the onion in the fat 8 minutes, adding the garlic for the last 2.
Return the lamb and its juices.
Add the stock, russets, bay, thyme, remaining pepper and the rest of the salt.
Cover and simmer gently 1 hour.
Add the red potatoes and carrot.
Simmer uncovered 45 minutes, until the lamb is tender and the russets have collapsed into the broth.
Remove the bay leaves, taste and salt again.
Cool completely and freeze flat in two bags.
To serve, put the stew in a pot with the Guinness at the start so the alcohol cooks off.
Loosen with stock, a splash at a time, until spoonable.
Cover and heat on low 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Taste and salt.
Top with parsley and serve with sourdough and butter.
recipes.notes: Made 4 days ahead and frozen. Sets very thick when cold; thin with stock on reheating.

recipes.title: Kofta (Beef and Lamb Logs)

ingredients: 5 g cumin seed, toasted and ground
3 g coriander seed, toasted and ground
groups.name: Spice blend (20 g, for 2 lb meat)

ingredients: 1 medium yellow onion (about 150 g), grated and wrung to about 80 g pulp
groups.name: Meat mix

ingredients: Sumac and Aleppo pepper for the table
groups.name: To serve

steps: Toast the cumin and coriander seed in a dry pan over medium heat for 60 to 90 seconds until fragrant.
Cool the toasted seeds completely.
Grind the cumin, coriander, peppercorns and allspice; mix with the paprika, Aleppo, oregano, cinnamon and sumac. Do not toast the paprika, Aleppo or sumac.
Grate the onion on the fine side of a box grater and wring the pulp hard in a towel.
Combine the beef, lamb, onion pulp, garlic, 20 g spice blend, salt and MSG.
Knead by hand 3 to 5 minutes until the mix is tacky and pulls at your fingers.
Fry a teaspoon-sized test patty and adjust seasoning.
Portion into 16 logs of 2 oz, about 1 inch thick and 4 to 5 inches long, with blunt ends.
Smooth any surface cracks with wet hands.
Chill at least 1 hour, or wrap individually and freeze flat.
Double-skewer each cold log on bamboo skewers.
Grill over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes, turning 2 or 3 times, with one burner off as a cool zone for flare-ups.
Pull at 160°F internal.
Warm the pita on the grate 30 seconds a side.
Build each wrap with one log, grilled vegetables, yogurt sauce, pickled onions and a squeeze of charred lemon.
recipes.notes: Logs can be mixed and frozen days ahead; frozen 2 oz logs thaw quickly in a cooler. Spice blend keeps for months in a jar. Cook all logs at camp rather than bringing raw meat home. To make 4 lb, double everything including salt and spice.

recipes.title: Kofta Spice Blend (Aleppo, Weighed)
steps: Toast only the cumin and coriander seed in a dry pan over medium heat, 60 to 90 seconds, until fragrant.
Cool completely before grinding.
Grind the cumin, coriander, peppercorns and allspice together.
Crumble in the oregano by hand.
Mix in the paprika, Aleppo, cinnamon and sumac without toasting them.
Jar it.
recipes.notes: Keeps for months in a jar. Salt (15 g kosher) and MSG (2 to 3 g) go into the meat separately, not into the jar. Double for 4 lb of meat.

recipes.title: Kofta Spice Blend (Scalable, by Volume)
recipes.yield: seasons 2 lb meat (1 lb beef + 1 lb lamb)
steps: Mix all spices together.
Add directly to 1 lb ground beef plus 1 lb ground lamb.

recipes.title: Lemon Herb Compound Butter
steps: Whip the butter with the zest, herbs, salt and pepper.
Add the lemon juice slowly while whipping so it does not break.
Roll into a log in parchment.
Chill.
Slice coins at camp.
recipes.notes: Keeps chilled in the cooler through the weekend.

recipes.title: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice
recipes.yield: about 7.5 qt beans (8 qt stock pot)

ingredients: 1200 g kidney and pinto beans, sorted and rinsed
groups.name: Brine soak

ingredients: 700 g andouille sausage, sliced into coins
20 g no-salt Creole seasoning (Tony Chachere's no-salt)
1500 g water, plus more as needed
groups.name: Pot

ingredients: 20 g kosher salt (to start), plus more to taste
groups.name: Finish

ingredients: 900 g long-grain white or jasmine rice
groups.name: To serve

steps: Dissolve the soaking salt in the soaking water, add the beans, and soak covered at room temperature 8 to 24 hours.
Drain and rinse the beans.
Heat the lard in the stock pot over medium-high.
Brown the andouille in batches and remove to a plate, leaving the fat.
Add the onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook over medium, scraping up the fond, until soft, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, Creole seasoning, thyme, cayenne, and black pepper; stir until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the beans, ham hock, stock, water, and bay leaves.
Bring to a full rolling boil and hold it there for at least 10 minutes.
Drop to a low simmer, partially covered, stirring occasionally and scraping the bottom, about 90 minutes, until the beans are fully tender.
Top up with water as needed to keep the beans just covered, staying below the fill line.
Remove the hock and bay leaves; shred the meat, discard skin and bone, and return the meat to the pot with the andouille.
Mash about a third of the beans against the side of the pot (or pulse briefly with an immersion blender).
Simmer uncovered, stirring often, until thick and creamy, about 30 minutes.
Stir in the 20 g salt and the MSG, wait a couple of minutes, then taste a whole bean and add more salt in 5 g hits as needed.
Stir in the hot sauce.
Cook the rice according to package directions.
Serve the beans over rice topped with green onion and parsley.
recipes.notes: Freeze without rice, green onion, or parsley for up to 3 months; add them fresh when reheating. Thickens a lot when cold; thin with water when reheating and stir often to prevent scorching. Freeze flat in gallon bags filled about half (about 2 qt).

recipes.title: Low Country Seafood Boil

ingredients: Kosher salt, only if the water needs it after tasting
groups.name: Water

ingredients: 1.8 kg (4 lb) andouille, cut into 1 to 1.5 inch coins on the bias
5.4 kg (12 lb) snow crab clusters, frozen
2.7 kg (6 lb) raw shell-on headless shrimp (16/20 or 21/25), frozen
groups.name: Cook

ingredients: 900 g Garlic Old Bay Butter, melted
~500 ml boil liquor, from the pot
groups.name: Butter toss

steps: Fill the 80-qt pot to the 10-gallon line.
Add the Zatarain's, Old Bay, onions, lemons and garlic.
Light the burner at T-90; lid on only while bringing the water up from cold. Allow 45 to 60 minutes to a rolling boil.
Boil 5 to 10 minutes, then taste: it should taste like aggressively seasoned soup. Add kosher salt if it does not.
Lid off for the entire cook. Burner on full the entire time.
0:00: add the potatoes and andouille.
Watch for boilover once the potatoes go in; knock the burner down if foam climbs.
0:08: add the corn, mushrooms and frozen crab.
0:16: add the frozen shrimp, or once the pot is back to a full boil, whichever is later.
0:19: ladle out ~500 ml of boil liquor and stir it into the melted garlic Old Bay butter.
Kill the gas. Pull the basket and drain it.
Return the food to the empty, still-hot pot.
Pour the butter and boil liquor over the top, sprinkle the 60 g Old Bay over in two or three passes, and toss with the paddle about 10 minutes.
Pour off everything that pools at the bottom into bowls for the table as the dip.
recipes.notes: Melt the butter after any other prep, while the pot climbs. Keep warm until the toss. Hold tiny creamer potatoes until 0:05. Serve on a paper-covered table with Cajun butter, drawn lemon butter, cocktail sauce, remoulade, serrano ranch and the pickle bowls.

recipes.title: Make-Ahead Breakfast Burritos (Bacon, Sausage, Mushroom)

ingredients: 2 yellow onions, diced (just under 2 lb vegetables total)
groups.name: Burrito vegetables

ingredients: 8 oz cream cheese, cut into small cubes
groups.name: Sheet pan eggs

ingredients: Per burrito: about 2 Tbsp bean paste, 7 to 9 tots, 1/3 cup rice, scant 1/2 cup (about 100 g) egg mixture, 1 slice American or 1/4 cup shredded cheese
Per burrito, one of: 3 Tbsp (about 20 g) bacon, 1/4 cup (about 40 g) sausage, or 1/4 cup (about 44 g) mushrooms
groups.name: Assembly

steps: Cover the bacon lardons with water in a pan, boil the water off, then let them render and crisp in their own fat; drain.
Crumble and brown the sausage, ideally in the bacon pan; cool on a sheet pan.
Dry-sear the mushrooms in batches in stainless until their water is gone and they brown.
Off the heat, toss the mushrooms with the butter, salt and cilantro.
Toss the diced peppers, poblano and onions with the oil and taco seasoning until every piece is glossy.
Roast the vegetables at 400°F on uncrowded sheet pans until dry and caramelized.
Line a half sheet pan with parchment and spread the roasted vegetables over it.
Dot the cream cheese cubes over the vegetables.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper just to uniform yellow and pour over.
Bake at 325°F 30 to 35 minutes, checking at 25 and rotating once, until the center is just set with a slight wobble.
Cut the egg slab into quarters on the pan to speed cooling.
For the bean paste, cook the onion, garlic and poblano in the oil and butter until very soft.
Add the beans, salt, pepper and cayenne or Aleppo, then blend smooth to a stiff, spreadable paste.
Fry the tots darker than you would eat them, salt them hot, and cool on a rack.
Heat the rice pouches, spread thin on a sheet pan to cool fast, and refrigerate.
Cool every component completely.
Warm tortillas in stacks of 8 wrapped in foil at 350°F for 10 to 12 minutes; warm only one stack at a time.
Smear bean paste over a 6 by 4 inch patch about 3 to 4 inches from the near edge.
Layer tots, rice, egg mixture and the meat or mushroom on the beans in a 6-inch line.
Top with the cheese.
Fold in the sides and roll tight.
Wrap in 12 by 10.75 inch foil sheets and label the foil with a Sharpie by filling and cheese.
Refrigerate 12 for the first morning and freeze 12 for the second.
At camp, reheat on a cool zone of the grill, turning every few minutes.
recipes.notes: Make extra filling; 24 burritos ran short on bacon and sausage. Frozen burritos hold 1 to 3 months; overwrap the foil with a freezer bag and reheat from frozen in foil at 350°F about 40 minutes.

recipes.title: Mild Chili with Toasted Dried Chiles

ingredients: 28 g dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded (about 4)
30 g dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded (about 2)
1 dried morita chile, stemmed and seeded
455 g dark red kidney beans, rinsed and drained
455 g light red kidney beans, rinsed and drained
2 g dried Mexican oregano, whole leaf
groups.name: Chili

steps: Toast the guajillos, anchos and morita in a dry skillet over medium heat, pressing flat, about 30 seconds per side, until fragrant. Do not blacken.
Toast the cumin seeds in the same skillet until fragrant and a shade darker. Grind.
Cover the chiles with the boiling stock and soak 20 minutes.
Blend the chiles with the soaking liquid until smooth.
Brown the beef with the onion and garlic. Drain excess fat if desired.
Add the tomato paste and ground cumin and cook, stirring, until darkened.
Crush in the oregano.
Transfer to the slow cooker. Add the chile puree, both beans, tomatoes, poblano, jalapeno, salt, MSG, pepper and cracker crumbs. Stir.
If it looks tight, stir in more stock until it is a thick stew that settles when stirred.
Cook on low overnight, about 8 hours.
Portion half into flat freezer bags and freeze. Refrigerate the rest in shallow containers.
Reheat gently, adjust salt and serve with the toppings.
recipes.notes: Make 2 to 3 days ahead. Cool in shallow containers, not in the slow cooker insert. Freeze half flat in bags before anyone eats from the pot.

recipes.title: Mudslide Slushie Base (Adults)
steps: Whisk until the espresso powder dissolves.
Refrigerate.
Shake before pouring.
Run on the Milkshake preset, or the Spike setting.
Add Kahlua, Baileys or vodka at the glass.

recipes.title: Mulled Cider with Chairman's Spiced Rum

ingredients: peel of 2 oranges, in wide strips
groups.name: Concentrate (make ahead)

ingredients: Chairman's Reserve Spiced rum, at the mug
groups.name: To serve

steps: Simmer the water, sugar, cinnamon, allspice, cloves, ginger, orange peel and star anise for 20 minutes.
Steep off the heat 20 minutes more.
Strain.
Stir in the orange juice.
Jar and refrigerate.
Heat the cider with the concentrate until steaming, about 75°C. Do not boil.
Hold on Keep Warm (Instant Pot or Dutch oven on low), or pour into a pre-warmed airpot: boiling water in, 5 minutes, dump.
Pour rum into the mug first, then ladle the cider over it.
recipes.notes: Concentrate keeps for weeks in the fridge. Do not increase the cloves. One 84.5 oz airpot: about 0.6×. Hobbit weekend: 2×, served as two 1-gallon nights, with two 750 ml bottles of Chairman's for six adults.

recipes.title: Mushroom Duxelles Mix (for Foil Packets)

ingredients: 450 g mushrooms, half button and half portabella (gills scraped), minced to about 2 mm
5 g fresh thyme leaves (or 2 g dried)

steps: Scrape the gills from the portabellas.
Pulse the mushrooms in a food processor in two batches, bowl no more than half full, until about 2 mm and still distinct.
Cook in a dry pan over medium-high, stirring occasionally, until the released water evaporates and the mushrooms squeak and brown, 8 to 10 minutes or a little longer for portabella.
Add the butter, shallot, garlic and thyme and cook 2 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the cream cheese until evenly melted.
Check that a spoonful mounds and nothing runs when the pan is tilted; if it weeps, return to medium heat 2 to 3 minutes.
Season with the salt and pepper.
Cool and refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Holds refrigerated through the weekend.

recipes.title: Mushrooms on Toast with Soft Eggs
steps: Soft eggs: lower the eggs into boiling water and cook 6 minutes.
Move them straight into an ice bath for 5 minutes.
Peel gently under cool running water.
Refrigerate in a covered container with a damp paper towel over them.
To serve, put the eggs in a bowl, cover with water just off the boil and leave 4 minutes to warm through.
Mushrooms: get a wide pan properly hot with the lard.
Add the mushrooms in one layer and leave them alone 4 minutes.
Stir and keep cooking until browned and squeaky, 4 to 6 minutes more. Use two pans if crowded.
Salt the mushrooms.
Add the butter, garlic and thyme. Cook 1 minute.
Add the cream and reduce 2 minutes.
Taste and salt again.
Spoon over the toast and grate the cheddar over the top.
Halve the eggs, salt them and put them on the toast.
recipes.notes: Eggs cooked and peeled up to 3 days ahead; mushrooms sliced the day before.

recipes.title: Papas Arrugadas with Mojo Verde

ingredients: 1.5 kg small waxy potatoes, scrubbed, unpeeled
groups.name: Papas arrugadas

ingredients: 60 g cilantro, leaves and tender stems
groups.name: Mojo verde

steps: Mojo: blend everything but the oil until smooth.
With the blender running, pour in the oil.
Taste and keep salting until it tastes sharp and loud.
Jar the mojo.
Potatoes: put them in a wide pot in a single layer.
Add the salt and just enough water to barely cover.
Boil hard, uncovered, 20 to 25 minutes, until a knife slides in and the water has nearly gone.
Pour off whatever water is left.
Return the pot to low heat and shake it every 30 seconds, 3 to 5 minutes, until the potatoes are dry, the skins wrinkle and a white salt bloom forms.
Serve in the pot, scattered with chopped cilantro, with the mojo in ramekins alongside.
recipes.notes: Mojo made Tuesday; keeps a week refrigerated. Take the mojo out of the fridge about an hour before serving so the oil loosens.

recipes.title: Pico de Gallo

ingredients: 400 g roma tomatoes, seeded and diced

steps: Combine everything.
recipes.notes: Make the day it is served or the day before; it declines by the next day.

recipes.title: Poor Man's Cochon de Lait
recipes.yield: one 4.3 kg (9.47 lb) bone-in pork butt, pulled

ingredients: 15 to 25 g kosher salt, to taste
groups.name: Finish

steps: Whisk the butter, stock, hot sauce, Worcestershire, garlic powder, and onion powder until smooth; keep warm so the butter stays liquid.
Inject the pork all over in a 3 cm grid, going deep and pulling back slowly.
Wipe off excess injection.
Mix the Creole seasoning, salt, brown sugar, and black pepper and coat the pork on all sides.
Refrigerate uncovered on a rack 24 to 36 hours.
Heat the oven to 275°F (135°C).
Roast the pork fat side up on a rack in a roasting pan until the internal temperature reaches 200°F (93°C) and the bone pulls free, 9 to 11 hours.
Tent loosely with foil and rest 1 hour.
Pull the pork into shreds while still warm, discarding bone and large fat pockets.
Skim the fat from the pan drippings and toss the pork with the drippings.
Sprinkle the finishing salt over the pork in 5 g hits, tossing and tasting as you go.
recipes.notes: Needs a meat injector and a roasting pan with rack. Cool in shallow containers or flat bags and refrigerate within 2 hours. Freeze pulled pork with its drippings for up to 3 months; reheat with a splash of drippings or water.

recipes.title: Queso (American and Sharp Cheddar)

ingredients: 120 g sharp cheddar, grated from a block
3 g dry mustard (Colman's), or 10 g Dijon

steps: Whisk the mustard into the evaporated milk.
Warm the milk mixture over low heat.
Add the American cheese in handfuls, stirring constantly, until smooth.
Off the heat, stir in the cheddar a handful at a time until melted.
Season with white pepper, adding salt only if needed.
Cool and refrigerate.
At camp, reheat in a dutch oven at the edge of the coals until molten, then hold in a crockpot on warm.
recipes.notes: Reheats without breaking. Use block cheddar, not bagged shredded.

recipes.title: Quick Pickled Red Onions

ingredients: 2 red onions, about 400 g, sliced thin

steps: Pack the onions into a quart jar.
Bring the vinegar, water, sugar and salt to a simmer, stirring until dissolved.
Pour over the onions and press them under.
Cool, lid and refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Ready in an hour, keeps two weeks refrigerated. For the ploughman's board.

recipes.title: Quick Pickled Red Onions (Camping Batch)
steps: Pack the sliced onions into a jar.
Boil the vinegar, water, sugar and salt.
Pour the hot brine over the onions.
Cool, then refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Ready in an hour, better after two days, better still at a week. Also made for the Aug 2026 kofta trip, where no quantities were recorded.

recipes.title: Rajma (Kidney Bean Curry)

ingredients: 1247 g kidney and pinto beans, sorted and rinsed
groups.name: Brine soak

ingredients: 3500 g water, plus more as needed
groups.name: Beans

steps: Dissolve the soaking salt in the soaking water, add the beans, and soak covered at room temperature about 12 hours.
Drain and rinse the beans.
Add the beans, cooking water, and bay leaves to the stock pot.
Bring to a full rolling boil and hold it there for at least 10 minutes.
Drop to a low simmer, partially covered, until fully tender, about 75 minutes. Do not drain.
While the beans simmer, heat the ghee in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium.
Add the cumin seeds, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, and cloves; stir until the cumin darkens, about 1 minute.
Add the onion and cook over medium to medium-high, stirring often, until deep amber-brown with darker edges, 20 to 30 minutes; add a splash of water if the bottom catches.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the ginger, garlic, and serranos and cook until the raw smell is gone, about 2 minutes.
Add the Kashmiri chili powder, coriander, ground cumin, and turmeric with a splash of water; stir constantly for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and the 10 g salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until thick and the fat separates at the edges, about 15 minutes.
Remove the cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, and cloves from the masala.
Remove the bay leaves from the bean pot.
Scrape the masala into the beans.
Mash about a quarter of the beans against the side of the pot or with an immersion blender.
Simmer uncovered, stirring often, about 30 minutes, until the gravy coats a spoon.
Stir in the garam masala and the kasuri methi crushed between your palms.
Stir in the butter over low heat until emulsified.
Add the 45 g salt and the MSG, tasting a whole bean as you go.
Rinse the rice well, soak 20 minutes, drain, and cook according to package directions.
Finish with lemon juice and cilantro and serve over rice.
recipes.notes: Freeze without rice or cilantro for up to 3 months; the garam masala, methi, butter, and salt can go in before freezing. Add a fresh squeeze of lemon when reheating. Keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Ras el Hanout with Caraway (No Cardamom)

ingredients: 1/4 tsp caraway seed, toasted and ground

steps: If using whole caraway, cumin or coriander, toast in a dry pan and grind.
Whisk all spices together until evenly combined.
Transfer to an airtight jar.
recipes.notes: Keeps 3 to 6 months in an airtight jar; ginger and cinnamon fade fastest. Requested scaling to a 0.14 oz container was never completed.

recipes.title: Red Beans (Thick, for Foil Packets)

ingredients: 1 can (15.5 oz) red kidney beans, rinsed and drained
60 g green bell pepper, diced 5 mm

steps: Sweat the onion, celery and bell pepper in the butter over medium 6 to 8 minutes, until soft with no color.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the paprika, thyme and cayenne for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, broth and bay leaves and simmer uncovered 15 to 20 minutes.
Pull the bay leaves.
Blend about two-thirds of the batch with an immersion blender, leaving the rest whole.
Reduce until a spoon dragged across the bottom leaves a track that holds 2 seconds.
Season with the salt and pepper.
Cool and refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Must be thick and scoopable so it does not pool in a sealed foil packet.

recipes.title: Reese's Puffs Krispie Treats with Orange Dark Chocolate Drizzle

ingredients: 1 to 2 tsp neutral or coconut oil
1/4 tsp orange extract (or 2 to 3 drops orange oil)
groups.name: Orange chocolate drizzle

steps: Butter or line the pan and measure both cereals into a big bowl.
Melt the butter in a large pot over low-medium heat.
Add the marshmallows and salt and stir until smooth.
Off the heat, stir in the peanut butter until streak-free.
Fold in both cereals quickly until coated.
Press gently into the pan with a buttered spatula.
Let set about 25 minutes, then cut.
Melt the chocolate with the oil low and slow.
Off the heat, stir in the extract, then the zest.
Drizzle over the cut bars.
Sprinkle with flaky salt.
Chill 15 minutes to set.

recipes.title: Reese's Puffs No-Bake Clusters
steps: Line a tray with wax paper and measure the cereal into a large bowl.
Combine the butter, milk, sugar, peanut butter and cocoa in a large skillet over medium heat, stirring until smooth.
Bring to a full rolling boil, then boil exactly 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Off the heat, stir in the vanilla.
Pour over the cereal and fold quickly until coated.
Scoop onto wax paper or press into a lined 8x8 pan.
Cool about 25 minutes until set.
recipes.notes: Press a few dry Puffs onto the tops right after scooping for crunch.

recipes.title: Remoulade
steps: Finely chop the cornichons and capers.
Stir everything together.
Refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Holds two weeks refrigerated and improves sitting.

recipes.title: Roast Cornish Game Hens with Garlic Thyme Butter
steps: Hen butter: mash the butter, garlic, thyme, lemon zest and pepper together, roll in parchment and refrigerate.
Take the hens out of their packaging over the sink and pat dry.
Salt with the 53 g salt between the seven, inside and out.
Set on sheet pans breast side up and refrigerate uncovered overnight.
Take the hen butter out of the fridge an hour before so it softens.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Pat the hens dry.
Rub the butter under and over the skin.
Put a lemon quarter in each cavity and tie the legs.
Nestle 4 hens on one pan of parboiled roast potatoes and 3 on the other.
Roast at 425°F, swapping racks and rotating pans after 30 minutes, until the thighs read 165°F (about 55 minutes).
Rest 15 minutes under foil.
recipes.notes: Hen butter keeps several days refrigerated. Roast on top of the duck fat roast potatoes. Strain the rendered hen fat and keep it for frying.

recipes.title: Roast Hen Gravy

ingredients: pan juices from the roast hens
groups.name: To finish

steps: Cook the butter and flour together 2 minutes.
Whisk in the stock and simmer 5 minutes until smooth.
Season with the 4 g salt and black pepper, to just under where you'd want it.
Cool and jar.
Pour the hen pan juices into a jar and let the fat rise.
Warm the base in a saucepan and whisk in the defatted juices.
Simmer 5 minutes.
Taste and finish the seasoning.
Strain the remaining hen fat into a jar for later frying.
recipes.notes: Base made 3 days ahead; seasoned light because the juices from the salted hens bring the rest.

recipes.title: Salsa Roja de Árbol (Full Hot)

ingredients: 25 g chiles de árbol, toasted and stemmed, seeds in
4 dried guajillo chiles, toasted, stemmed and seeded

steps: Toast the árbols and guajillos in a dry pan 20 to 30 seconds a side, with the vent running.
Soak the chiles in hot water 20 minutes.
Line a sheet pan with foil and set the tomatoes cut side down with the onion and garlic.
Broil about 4 inches from the element, 10 minutes, until blackened in spots.
Peel the garlic.
Blend with the vinegar, salt, a splash of soaking liquid and the liquid pooled on the pan; leave it coarse.
Heat the oil until shimmering.
Pour in the salsa and fry 5 minutes, stirring, with the vent running.
Taste after frying and add more vinegar if flat.
Cool and refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Improves over a few days; frying helps it keep longer.

recipes.title: Sausage Rolls

ingredients: 2 eggs, beaten (1 for sealing, 1 with a splash of water for egg wash)

steps: Combine the pork, onion, sage, fennel, salt and pepper.
Fry a teaspoon and taste.
Divide into 8 portions, about 140 g each.
Unfold each pastry sheet, press the seams flat and cut in half into 2 strips.
Lay a log of filling down each strip, egg one edge, fold and seal with a fork.
Cut each strip into 4.
Freeze on a tray, then bag.
To bake, heat the oven to 400°F and line two sheet pans with parchment.
Lay the rolls flat from frozen, crimped edge to the side, about 2 cm apart.
Brush the tops with egg wash.
Bake 22 to 25 minutes, until deep golden and the filling reads 160°F.
Rest 5 minutes. Serve with HP and English mustard.
recipes.notes: Bake straight from frozen.

recipes.title: Serrano Ranch

ingredients: 3 serrano chiles, minced fine (seeds and ribs in for heat)

steps: Mince the serranos fine, leaving seeds and ribs in on at least two.
Stir everything together, thinning with the buttermilk.
Refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Make no more than 3 days ahead; buttermilk will not hold a week. Ride in the cooler.

recipes.title: Skillet Cornbread with Honey Butter

ingredients: 70 g lard, melted and cooled slightly
groups.name: Cornbread

steps: Whisk the butter, 45 g honey and 2 g salt for the honey butter until smooth. Refrigerate.
Put 45 g lard in the skillet and heat the oven to 425F with the skillet inside.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Whisk the buttermilk, eggs and 21 g honey, then whisk in the melted lard.
Fold wet into dry just until no dry pockets remain. The batter stays lumpy.
Rest the batter 15 minutes.
Swirl the hot lard up the sides of the skillet, pour in the batter and return to the oven.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until golden with deep brown edges and a clean skewer.
Cool in the pan.
Before serving, rewarm in the skillet at 350F for 10 minutes.
Finish with flaky salt and serve with the honey butter.
recipes.notes: Honey butter can be made a day ahead; take it out 2 to 3 hours before serving to soften. Leftover wedges are split and griddled for breakfast sandwiches.

recipes.title: Slow Cooker Carnitas
recipes.yield: 4 kg deboned pork shoulder (7 qt slow cooker)

ingredients: 4000 g pork shoulder meat (from a 9.88 lb bone-in shoulder), deboned and cut into 5 cm chunks
groups.name: Dry brine

steps: Toss the pork with the salt, oregano, cumin, and black pepper.
Refrigerate covered overnight.
Place the onion, garlic, and bay leaves in the slow cooker and add the pork.
Pour over the orange juice, lime juice, oil, and water.
Tuck in the spent orange halves (do not add lime halves).
Cover and cook on low about 10 hours, until fork-tender.
Discard the orange halves, onion, and bay leaves.
Break the pork into large shreds with two forks, keeping some chunks.
Skim the fat from the juices and reserve both separately.
To serve, heat a cast iron skillet over high with a spoonful of the reserved fat.
Add pork in a single layer with a splash of the juices and cook undisturbed until the liquid evaporates and the bottom is crisp, about 5 minutes.
recipes.notes: Needs a 7 qt or larger slow cooker. Freeze shredded, uncrisped pork with some of its fat and juices for up to 3 months; crisp after thawing. Freeze the bone for stock.

recipes.title: SlushiMax Margarita (Spiked Slush Max)
recipes.yield: 112 oz, about 12 servings at 9 oz, about 15% ABV

ingredients: 59 oz Master of Mixes Margarita mix (the full 1.75 L bottle)
10 oz unsweetened lime juice (fresh or 100% bottled, not Rose's or sweetened)

steps: Chill every ingredient before it goes in the vessel.
Pour everything into the Ninja SlushiMax vessel.
Run on Spiked Slush Max.
Run the rinse cycle before switching to another batch.
recipes.notes: If the first taste reads too sweet, lime is the lever. If it won't freeze, add 1/4 cup water or soda per serving and give it 30 more minutes.

recipes.title: SlushiMax Spiced Strawberry Daiquiri (Spiked Slush Max)
recipes.yield: 112 oz, about 12 servings at 9 oz, about 16% ABV

ingredients: 59 oz Master of Mixes Strawberry Daiquiri mix (the full 1.75 L bottle)
8 oz unsweetened lime juice (fresh or 100% bottled, not Rose's or sweetened)

steps: Chill every ingredient before it goes in the vessel.
Pour everything into the Ninja SlushiMax vessel.
Run on Spiked Slush Max.
Run the rinse cycle before switching to another batch.
recipes.notes: No cilantro in this one. If it won't freeze, add 1/4 cup water or soda per serving and give it 30 more minutes.

recipes.title: Split Buttermilk Pancakes (Sweet and Ham-Cheddar) with Griddle Eggs

ingredients: 8 oz plain smoked ham (not honey glazed), 5 mm dice
groups.name: Toppings at the pour

ingredients: About 1 lb 10 oz breakfast sausage (the rest of a 2.5 lb purchase after the burritos)
12 eggs, blended 10 to 15 seconds, in 2 squeeze bottles
groups.name: Griddle

steps: At home, whisk each dry blend and bag it in a labeled 2-gallon freezer bag.
At home, whisk the buttermilk, egg and cooled melted butter for each wet container.
At camp, cook the sausage on the griddle first.
Pour one wet mix into each dry bag and squeeze until just hydrated, leaving lumps.
Rest the batter 15 minutes.
Add butter to the griddle if the sausage fat looks thin.
For ham pancakes, crisp the ham dice on the griddle and nudge into loose rounds.
Cut a corner of the savory bag and pour batter over each ham round; scatter cheddar on the wet top.
For sweet pancakes, pour on the griddle and scatter chocolate chips or blueberries on the wet top.
Flip once and cook through.
After the pancakes are off, turn the griddle to low.
Melt the 60 g butter, add the eggs, and push slowly with a spatula until just set and still glossy.
recipes.notes: Wet mixes keep a couple of days refrigerated; shake hard before pouring since the butter sets into flecks. Blended eggs hold in squeeze bottles in the cooler.

recipes.title: Tartar Sauce
steps: Stir everything together.
Taste and salt again. It should be sharp enough to cut fried batter.
Jar and refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Keeps a week refrigerated.

recipes.title: Ted's Zaza 72-Hour Pizza Dough
recipes.yield: three ~318 g balls (12 to 13 inch pies) or two ~477 g balls

ingredients: 270 g water (250 g up front, 20 g held for bassinage)
groups.name: Final dough

steps: Day 1, ~9pm: disperse the 0.15 g yeast in the 80 g water, then stir in the 80 g flour.
Mix 5 g mother with 30 g flour and 30 g water to a paste.
Leave both at ~70F for 12 hours.
Day 2, ~9am: check the levain is roughly doubled and a spoonful floats; give it 2 to 3 more hours if not.
Mix the 470 g flour, malt and 0.15 g yeast in a large bowl.
Add 250 g water and 30 g levain to the poolish and stir to loosen.
Combine wet into dry and mix about 3 minutes until no dry flour remains.
Cover and rest 1 hour.
Add the salt and the reserved 20 g water; squeeze and fold about 1 minute until absorbed.
Work in the olive oil until it disappears.
Rest 1 hour at 70 to 75F.
Check dough temperature: target 70 to 75F.
Divide into three ~318 g pieces (or two ~477 g).
Ball each tightly with a sealed seam.
Place each in a lightly oiled 2-qt round container and lid.
Rest 30 minutes at room temperature, then refrigerate at 36 to 40F for 72 to 96 hours.
Bake day: pull the containers 2 to 3 hours ahead to come fully to room temperature.
Preheat the steel 6 to 8 inches below the broiler at 550F for 60 minutes; switch to broil for the last 10 minutes.
Shape by hand from the center out, leaving a 1-inch rim. No rolling pin.
Launch from a semolina-dusted wood peel, dressing in under 60 seconds.
Bake 5 to 7 minutes, rotating halfway.
recipes.notes: Label containers with date and time. Past 96 hours the dough goes slack. Refresh the mother (20 g mother, 40 g flour, 20 g water) in the same session as the levain build.

recipes.title: The Full English

ingredients: two 415 g cans Heinz British baked beans
120 g duck fat, plus strained hen fat

steps: Par-cook the brats the day before: bare simmer in well-salted water 10 minutes until firm, then cool and refrigerate.
Lay the bacon on wire racks set in sheet pans and bake at 400°F.
After 10 minutes, add the brats on a second pan. Bake both 15 minutes more, until the bacon is crisp and the brats browned.
Fry the bread in duck fat until golden on both sides and salt it.
Hold the bacon and brats under foil.
Toss the mushrooms in bacon fat from under the racks, salt them hard and spread in one layer on a half sheet pan.
Broil 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes cut side up, brushed with bacon fat and salted.
Broil 4 to 5 minutes more, until the tomatoes blister and the mushrooms brown.
Warm the beans in a small pot.
Fry the eggs in butter last, over medium, in batches.
Plate everything at once, beans in a ramekin on each plate.

recipes.title: Tomato Soup

ingredients: 1.6 kg whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes (two 28 oz cans)
5 g sugar, if the tomatoes taste sharp
groups.name: Soup

steps: Melt the butter with the olive oil over medium heat.
Cook the onion with a pinch of the salt until soft and golden, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes with their juice, the stock, remaining salt, pepper, oregano, thyme, bay leaves and Parmesan rind.
Simmer uncovered 30 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves, any thyme stems and the rind.
Blend until smooth. Add the sugar only if needed.
Cool in shallow containers and refrigerate.
To serve, reheat gently, stir in the cream and tear in the basil.
recipes.notes: Make up to 4 days ahead. Hold the cream and basil until reheating. Served with grilled cheese.

recipes.title: Vinegar Slaw
steps: Whisk the vinegar, sugar, oil, salt, celery seed and pepper.
Pour over the cabbage and carrot and toss.
Refrigerate.
recipes.notes: Make about 3 days ahead; it improves, but goes limp by 5 days.
